questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the time the exchange was a mandatory, and the destination was already determined seeing as I was a Korean studies undergrad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To be honest I arrived before time, and due to that it was hard to find information. National health insurance and arc/residence card are things your host university tell you about at the orientation they give.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You could apply to get a buddy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think they should have been a little more transparent about which courses we are restricted from taking as exchange students and also based on our major.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little hard but okay. We found the place through Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's more freedom but know that for people you attend classes with the other international students know each other from the on-campus dorms, so you might lose out a bit in terms of more natural opportunities to get along with others. However, living off-campus means no curfew, no room checks and you are able to get visitors without having to get approval. But depending on the state of you Airbnb and your host, you might also be in for having to make time for being home for electricity/water measuring and for welcoming repairmen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think if you are out early it can be very satisfying.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had problems with registering and had to call the school. Later in the day we were then able to register but at that point a lot of courses were taken.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cannot really remember the steps to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We ended up going to the International Office that helped us register for the last classes we needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We definitely had some challenges and were rejected twice from two different classes. For one of the classes we were told that the professor noticed that we did not have the right major to apply, but we were not made aware of the restriction and it wasn't written anywhere on the website when we registered for the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a really good look at the guide for registering because the courses disappear quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think finding courses was really hard because there were certain requirements from Copenhagen University and restrictions at Sungshin as well. However, maybe we were a little worse off compared to how it would be for others due to the problems we had with the website and being unable to register in the beginning.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: "Korean Language School, Regular Course" and "International Relations of East Asia" were very intense. The former was the mandatory language school we had to attend, and we regularly had written and oral tests each week. And the workload was a lot. "International Relations of East Asia" was a political course, and the professor actually told us that it was better if we were political science majors. It was very heavy and for a lot of words and concepts we had to do our own research. The workload was heavy and especially leading up to the midterms and finals.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is quite different at Sungshin from that of UCPH. I think it is more free at our university vs. that of Sungshin. Everything seemed a bit rigid. In addtion, it was also more passive or at least that was true for our poltical course where we were mostly listening.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Korean Language School, Regular Course
International Seminar: Korean and Global Affairs (001)
International Relations of East Asia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
As the language course is mandatory I won't comment on that. 
So I would say the "International Seminar: Korean and Global Affairs (001)" was a really nice course. The workload was lesser than the other two but it was a course where you got to know the other students learn about their cultures and way of thinking. In addition, we also learned about Korean culture and society.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The university had their own mandatory insurance. On top of the national health insurance, the university required you to pay for their insurance as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: If you cook at home groceries can be a little expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The festival was fun but we weren't really told about any clubs or social events we could join. I think the buddy program was probably good as well, I just did not join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure. The festival had been pushed due to covid restrictions so I experienced it but usually it would be during summer I think. As for other events I'm unsure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you go to Sungshin I think it's better to join the buddy program, because the people with buddies were more aware of any events at the school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye out for any exciting events in Seoul on social media and go out and do the classic stuff. Go to famous spots in Seoul, amusement parks, exhibitions, foodmarkets etc. Make sure to make the most of it while you are there, and if you have the energy for it do some trips during the weekends or holidays and go outside of Seoul.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite okay but I probably found it easier due to my major.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't really have a tip but the easiest is probably to try and socialize with them through class or clubs. And if those aren't an option then the buddy program.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Intially the staring. People stare a lot, and in the beginning it's hard to get used to. There is typically no malicious intent behind it, they are just curious.
And one funny thing is how they mix sweet and savory. I experienced getting syrup in my blt sandwich, syrup with my pizza and I heard about people getting garlic bread with sugar on top.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food culture. I liked going to Korean restaurants and having a variety of side dishes and in general I really liked the food. Sometimes they might get a little too experimental with their food but they are often spot on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is a smaller university so they are more inclined to help you at the international office. 
However, don't expect to be able to take any courses you want.
Definitely, participate in the buddy program or actively find something else social.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is located on top of a hill...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting the language course certificate! You put in so much work and it so intense through the semester, so getting the certificate was really rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The intensity of the language course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
